headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: Haystack’s broad egress/MCP can feed a shell-capable, filesystem-writing content agent that also handles secrets.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Haystack can call MCP servers and REST APIs, so if its outputs are bridged into the course agent’s stdin/stdout or files, attacker-controlled content could be treated as instructions. The course agent reads/writes the filesystem and runs subprocesses, increasing the chance of unsafe parsing. No direct shared channel is documented, so this is inferred.
conditions: IF Haystack output is copied into files or stdin/stdout consumed by the course agent
IF an MCP server returns untrusted text that the course agent parses as instructions
mitigations: Add a manual review step before the course agent consumes Haystack output
Restrict Haystack MCP endpoints to trusted sources only
Use a strict output schema for Haystack responses
Disable automatic execution of any instructions found in retrieved text
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Haystack has broad network egress and MCP access, while the course agent touches configuration secrets and can read/write the filesystem. If they share a workspace or the course agent ingests Haystack outputs, secrets or paper data can be exfiltrated through Haystack’s outbound paths. The pairwise leakage pathway is plausible from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF both agents run in the same workspace or container network
IF the course agent exposes configuration secrets to files or prompts that Haystack can access
IF Haystack forwards retrieved content to external APIs
mitigations: Separate the agents into distinct containers and volumes
Remove secrets from any shared directory
Block Haystack egress except to approved endpoints
Rotate exposed secrets before co-running the pair
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss prevention

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Haystack can use MCP and broad egress, while the course agent can execute shell commands, install packages, spawn subprocesses, and write files. Even without modify_git_state, they can still contend over the same filesystem or runtime resources if co-located. The profiles do not state locking or isolation, so conflict is plausible in default local development setups.
conditions: IF both agents share a writable directory
IF the course agent installs packages or writes artifacts while Haystack reads the same paths
IF the orchestrator does not provide file locking
mitigations: Use separate working directories for each agent
Run package installs in an isolated environment
Disable shared writable mounts
Schedule non-overlapping runs
requires-engineering: add locking around shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Haystack is a search/RAG agent, so its retrieved text can become input to the course agent’s writing or agentic workflows. The course agent exposes /ask and /agentic-ask style surfaces and can act on content, so unverified Haystack output may cascade into downstream actions. No verification step is documented between them.
conditions: IF Haystack output is fed into the course agent’s ask or agentic-ask endpoints
IF the course agent uses retrieved text as authoritative without citation checks
mitigations: Require citation checks before the course agent acts on Haystack output
Insert a human approval step for agentic actions
Limit Haystack to retrieval-only mode
Log source provenance alongside every generated claim
requires-engineering: add automated fact verification

E_compliance.rationale: Haystack touches anonymous usage statistics, while the course agent handles academic papers, metadata, research questions, and configuration secrets. If the pair is used on regulated or institutionally sensitive research data, the course agent’s local-development and secret-handling setup can create retention and residency mismatches. The profiles do not show matching compliance controls, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF regulated research data or personal data is processed through the course agent
IF logs or notebooks retain paper metadata or secrets beyond intended retention
IF the deployment crosses a residency boundary without a DPA
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in the shared workflow
Delete notebooks and logs after each run
Store secrets outside the project tree
Document retention and residency rules
requires-engineering: add compliance controls and audit logging
